messages:
Alex Park: FYI customer on prod saw repeated 504s + 'context canceled' from our Go SDK after ~15s. They say retries keep hitting upstream and everything stalls.
Maria Gomez: Is this the hosted API or Dedicated? Any repro or request snippet? :eyes:
Alex Park: Hosted. Attaching minimal repro we used in support -- they run many short requests concurrently and we saw connection resets. Code:
```
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 10,
  IdleConnTimeout: 2 * time.Second,
  DisableKeepAlives: false,
}
client := &http.Client{
  Transport: tr,
  Timeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewReader(payload))
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```
Alex Park: Note IdleConnTimeout is short because they thought it would free sockets faster.
Kevin Lee: Ah — two chances for cancellation: Request's ctx and client.Timeout. Also IdleConnTimeout 2s is tight for transient spikes. If a pooled conn is closed while request is waiting, net/http can return "connection reset by peer" or timeouts during header wait. Repeats + retries can exhaust dial concurrency.
Jordan Reed: Also check retries wrapper: if we do retries at SDK layer by calling client.Do(req) multiple times with same req without recreating body or using GetBody, second attempt will fail because body is drained. Do we rebuild the req body on retry?
Alex Park: Good catch — the user's code sets req.Body once and we pass the same request to our retry logic. We see errors like "http: request body too large to rewind" in logs intermittently.
Maria Gomez: So combined effects: short IdleConnTimeout drops idle sockets -> more dials -> client.Timeout or ctx cancels if dial or headers slow -> retries attempt to reuse drained body -> immediate failure or weird errors.
Kevin Lee: Suggested fixes:
- Use Transport.IdleConnTimeout >= expected inter-request gap (e.g., 30s)
- Increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost to reduce dials
- Prefer Request.WithContext for per-call deadlines and avoid client.Timeout if you need fine-grained cancellation
- Implement retries that recreate requests or use req.GetBody so body can be rewound
- Instrument with net/http/httputil or enable transport-level logging
Jordan Reed: Quick repro steps for support to give customer:
1) Run simple Go program above but set IdleConnTimeout=1s and MaxIdleConnsPerHost=1
2) Send 200 concurrent short requests with 100ms spacing
3) Add a retry loop that reuses req without GetBody
4) Observe mix of context canceled and body rewind errors
Alex Park: I'm going to reach back to customer with these steps and propose a patch in our SDK to copy the request body for retries and expose sensible defaults for Transport in our client constructor.
SRE Bot: Created ticket INF-7213 for SDK retry/body-rewind + default transport tuning :ticket:
Maria Gomez: Thanks. If you want, I can draft the SDK change. Also we should add a note in docs about not setting very low IdleConnTimeouts for high QPS.
Alex Park: Perfect, thanks all. I'll update thread after customer verification. :thumbsup:
